# A finite value-only covariance correction, with its implemented law

This is an internally derived intermediate construction for N687. It is not the requested polylogarithmic compiler and is not a priority claim. It combines frozen R22's two-value action with standard Gaussian martingale and Stein identities. The authorized helper independently reconstructed the law bound and challenged the single-action version; its detailed argument is retained in `helper/CHALLENGE.md`.

Throughout, TV(P,Q)=sup_A |P(A)-Q(A)|. Matrix norms are operator or Frobenius as indicated. Exact Gaussian vectors, scalar square roots, arithmetic and whole-vector g values are the runtime primitives. All Hessians, covariance matrices and Stein kernels below are analysis objects, not algorithm inputs.

## 1. Class and acquired covariance action

Let g=grad F:R^d -> R^d be globally L-Lipschitz, F in C^{1,1}; nonconvex fields are allowed. Let mu=E g(G), Sigma=Cov(g(G)). Gaussian Poincare gives 0<=Sigma<=L^2 I. Define H_s(c)=E Dg(c+sZ), using the weak derivative in the proof only.

The R22 heat action on a supplied v!=0 is

    u=v/||v||,
    Zperp=Z0-(u.Z0)u,
    R=s sqrt(A1^2+A2^2+A3^2),
    J_s(c;v)=||v|| [g(c+sZperp+Ru)-g(c+sZperp-Ru)]/(2R).

It costs two g values and satisfies E[J_s(c;v)|c,v]=H_s(c)v and ||J_s(c;v)||<=L||v|| on every execution. For v=0 return zero. Null events R=0 can be assigned zero. The proof is the line-segment derivative identity and the classical representation U chi_3 ~ N(0,1) for independent U uniform[-1,1]. No limiting difference quotient is used.

Draw T uniform[0,1], C standard Gaussian, put c=sqrt(T) C and s=sqrt(1-T), and compose two independent heat actions at these SAME c,s:

    J_Sigma(v)=J_s^{(2)}(c; J_s^{(1)}(c;v)).

Uniform T can be generated from three scalar Gaussians by (1+A/sqrt(A^2+B^2+C^2))/2. The event T=1 is null. This operation uses FOUR g values.

**Covariance-action theorem.** For every supplied v independent of the fresh seeds,

    E[J_Sigma(v)|v]=Sigma v,
    ||J_Sigma(v)||<=L^2||v||.

To prove it, let B_t be Brownian motion. The martingale E[g(B_1)|B_t] has integrand H_sqrt(1-t)(B_t), so Ito isometry gives

    Sigma=integral_0^1 E[H_sqrt(1-t)(sqrt(t)C)^2]dt.

# Stronger ordinary alternative: stratified covariance-action times

This alternative was constructed and executed after the independent-time obstruction. The same authorized helper checked its law bound and the additional arguments below. Full independent proofs are retained in helper/STRATIFIED.md.

## Legal program and unchanged full-law theorem

Draw T_j independently uniform on [(j-1)/k,j/k], rather than all of [0,1]. Use a fresh Gaussian center and two fresh secant actions. Define

    M(t)=E[H_sqrt(1-t)(sqrt(t)C)^2],
    Sigma_j=k integral_((j-1)/k)^(j/k) M(t)dt.

Then E[J_j(v)|v]=Sigma_j v, ||J_j(v)||<=L^2||v||, and (1/k)sum Sigma_j=Sigma. The average action is EXACTLY unbiased. Individual calls are independent but not identically distributed. Conditioned on Z,

    E||Jbar(Z)-Sigma Z||^2
       =k^(-2)sum_j E||J_j(Z)-Sigma_j Z||^2 <=L^4||Z||^2/k.

Every step of THEOREM.md's bound (B) remains valid, with the same deterministic n+4k query cap. `corrected_sampler(..., stratified_time=True)` implements it. Exact mean is mu; covariance is sigma^2 I+E[Jbar Jbar^T]/(4 tau^2 n^2). The independent-time obstruction does not cover this variant.

## Matrix time-quadrature geometry

Let H_t=E[Dg(B_1)|F_t], a bounded self-adjoint matrix martingale. With M(t)=E H_t^2, for u>t,

    M(u)-M(t)=E[(H_u-H_t)^2] >=0,  0<=M(t)<=L^2 I.

The cross terms vanish conditionally; no commutativity is assumed. Thus M is Loewner monotone, including its weak-terminal endpoint. Every realized stratified average and integral Sigma lie between the same lower and upper matrix Riemann sums. Their difference telescopes, yielding pathwise

    ||(1/k)sum_j M(T_j)-Sigma||op <= L^2/k.                  (1)

This does not supply M(t) to the program. The sampled center and secant randomness remain acquired and charged.

## Exact sine-family variance reduction

For g_i=sin(x_i), put v=(1-exp(-2))/2 and q(t)=exp(-1)cosh t. The common-time coefficient qbar=(1/k)sum_j q(T_j) is unbiased for v. On a_j=(j-1)/k,b_j=j/k,

    E q(T_j)=exp(-1)k[sinh(b_j)-sinh(a_j)],
    E q(T_j)^2=exp(-2)[1/2+(k/4)(sinh(2b_j)-sinh(2a_j))].

Therefore

    Var(qbar)=exp(-2){(1/2+sinh(2)/4)/k-k[cosh(1/k)-1]
                      -(sinh(2)/2)tanh(1/(2k))}
              =c_star/k^3+O(k^(-5)),
    c_star=exp(-2)[sinh(2)-2]/48>0.

# Executed second positive correction

The n^(-2) deterministic covariance remainder can be removed by another ordinary binomial term without treating an action as a matrix. This finite acquired construction still has general d^(1/3) query rate. The independent audit and full coefficient proof are retained in helper/SECOND_ORDER.md.

Compose two fresh GLOBAL four-query covariance actions to obtain J^(2)(v), with E[J^(2)(v)|v]=Sigma^2v and ||J^(2)(v)||<=L^4||v||. This costs EIGHT original g values. The two actions have independent times and centers; reusing a center does not generally give Sigma^2.

With k first actions and ell second words, use separate fresh blocks conditional on retained Z and return

    Y2=gbar_n+tau Z-Jbar(Z)/(2tau n)
         -Jbar^(2)(Z)/(8tau^3 n^2)+eta W.                    (1)

Mean is exactly mu. Query cap is n+4k+8ell on every execution; arithmetic is O((n+k+ell)d), streaming storage O(d).

For the deterministic comparison set M2=tau I-Sigma/(2tau n)-Sigma^2/(8tau^3 n^2). Direct multiplication yields

    Sigma/n+M2^2+eta^2I=sigma^2I+Q2,
    Q2=Sigma^3/(8tau^4n^3)+Sigma^4/(64tau^6n^4)>=0.           (2)

Thus the Sigma^2 term cancels exactly. Keeping Q2 fixed in the covariance interpolation of THEOREM.md is valid for every n, because C_1=M2^2+eta^2I>=eta^2I and C_t=C_1+(1-t)Sigma/n. Conditional centered shift variance is at most

    d[L^4/(4tau^2n^2k)+L^8/(64tau^6n^4ell)].                 (3)

Cross terms vanish because the two correction blocks are independent given Z. The exact implemented law therefore obeys the safe bound

    TV(Y2,N(mu,sigma^2I))
      <=L^2 sqrt(d)/(2eta^2n^(3/2))+||Q2||F/(2eta^2)
        +d[L^4/(4tau^2n^2k)+L^8/(64tau^6n^4ell)]/(2eta^2).   (4)

For tau=eta=sigma/sqrt(2), r=L/sigma, a scalar upper bound is

    r^2 sqrt(d)/n^(3/2)+r^6 sqrt(d)/(2n^3)+r^8 sqrt(d)/(8n^4)
       +r^4d/(2n^2k)+r^8d/(8n^4ell).                        (5)

Only the FINAL operator of each second word may be ell-stratified while the first remains global: individual means Sigma_j Sigma then average to Sigma^2. Stratifying both operators at the same stratum would target a different mean of conditional squares and is not used.
